items.title: Reposition virtual sticks in landscape to prevent fighter occlusion
items.what: In widescreen/landscape view (Screenshot 9), the twin-stick control rings sit directly over the fighters' legs and feet, with the right stick completely occluding HasanAbi's lower right leg and mat contact point.
items.why: Point karate relies on reading distance, stance, and foot planting; placing dark circular controls directly over the character sprites destroys visual clarity and looks like an unadapted viewport bug.
items.how: Clamp the joysticks to the bottom-left and bottom-right viewport corners with lateral padding, or pull the Three.js camera back along the Z-axis in landscape media queries so the fighting plane remains clear of UI overlays.

items.title: Lower camera pitch to eliminate empty tatami expanse in portrait view
items.what: In portrait mode (Screenshots 3, 4, 5, 10), there is an empty band of tatami mat spanning roughly 25-30% of the screen height between the fighters' feet and the top boundary of the joystick dock.
items.why: The fighters appear pushed high and small in the frame, making touch interactions feel physically disconnected from the action while wasting prime screen real estate on featureless floor texture.
items.how: Lower the 3D camera height and decrease vertical pitch by 5-8 degrees to drop the horizon line, bringing the fighters closer to the lower-middle focal area and filling the upper frame with more dojo background architecture.

items.title: Dim or dismiss touch sticks during modal overlay states
items.what: On the Techniques screen (Screenshot 6), Settings screen (Screenshot 7), and bout card overlays (Screenshots 2 and 8), the full high-contrast twin-stick HUD remains brightly rendered at the bottom.
items.why: It creates severe visual clutter behind text-heavy screens and falsely implies the sticks are active touch targets while modals and countdowns are open.
items.how: Add an active modal state that fades the `#stick-container` opacity to 0.15 or translates it off-screen downward using a 200ms ease transition whenever a dialog or announcement banner is active.

items.title: Unify overlay typography with the cinematic brass display font
items.what: On the Qualifier and Match End screens (Screenshots 2, 8, and 11), the title uses a stylized geometric brass display font ('QUALIFIER'), immediately paired with standard neutral sans-serif ('vs HasanAbi') and generic caps body copy.
items.why: The abrupt jump to default sans-serif breaks the 80s martial arts tournament atmosphere and makes the opponent introduction text look like unstyled developer placeholder text.
items.how: Style the opponent name with the tournament display face or an elevated tracked condensed serif, adding subtle gold metallic gradient and drop-shadow styling consistent with the headline.

items.title: Center loading status text and increase progress bar visibility
items.what: On the initial boot screen (Screenshot 1), 'Starting up' is right-aligned above an extremely faint, hairline loading bar, while the ShoeMoney logo and footer text are centered.
items.why: The asymmetrical, right-aligned status label unbalances the portrait layout, and the low-contrast progress bar gives inadequate visual feedback during WebGPU shader compilation.
items.how: Center the 'Starting up' label directly above the bar, increase the progress track thickness from ~2px to 4px, and give the active progress fill a glowing amber tint (#E5A93C) matching the in-game HUD palette.
